I can't write `tasks.md` in this turn because your request rules out tool use, so the breakdown is below. Say the word and I'll save it as-is. I'm not reopening the plan. The open points it leaves are turned into short decision tasks so they don't block the build.

```markdown
# User Data Export: Implementation Tasks

Plan: build an API endpoint that exports all of a user's data. Use the easiest format. Should be fast. Ship next week.

## 0. Decisions (timebox: day 1, defaults apply if unanswered)
- [ ] T0.1 Format: default to JSON (easiest, and it is machine-readable).
- [ ] T0.2 Scope: inventory every data store and table holding user data. Default: all user-owned records, excluding other users' data and internal-only fields (password hashes, tokens, secrets).
- [ ] T0.3 Delivery: default to synchronous streaming response. Switch to async job + download link only if T2.3 shows exports exceed the time budget.
- [ ] T0.4 "Fast" target: set a concrete p95 (e.g. <5s for a typical user) so T5 has a pass/fail.

## 1. Data inventory
- [ ] T1.1 List all tables/collections/services that store user data.
- [ ] T1.2 Mark each field as include / exclude (secrets, internal flags, third-party data).
- [ ] T1.3 Write a per-source serializer interface (`export(user_id) -> iterator of records`).

## 2. Endpoint
- [ ] T2.1 Add route, e.g. `GET /api/users/me/export`.
- [ ] T2.2 Authentication: the caller can only export their own data. Admin/support access is out of scope unless T0 says otherwise.
- [ ] T2.3 Implement the aggregator that calls each serializer and streams JSON (avoid loading everything into memory).
- [ ] T2.4 Set response headers (`Content-Type`, `Content-Disposition: attachment`).
- [ ] T2.5 Error handling: a failing source returns a clear error rather than a silently partial export.

## 3. Security and privacy
- [ ] T3.1 Rate-limit the endpoint (e.g. a few requests per user per hour).
- [ ] T3.2 Require recent re-authentication or equivalent, since the export is a full data dump.
- [ ] T3.3 Audit-log each export (user, time, IP). Do not log the payload.
- [ ] T3.4 Confirm the export excludes other users' data and secrets.

## 4. Performance
- [ ] T4.1 Use indexed queries per user and paginate or stream large tables.
- [ ] T4.2 Run sources concurrently where safe.
- [ ] T4.3 Load-test with a large synthetic user.

## 5. Testing
- [ ] T5.1 Unit tests for each serializer.
- [ ] T5.2 Integration test: the export contains the expected data for a seeded user.
- [ ] T5.3 Authorization tests: unauthenticated and cross-user requests are rejected.
- [ ] T5.4 Performance check against the T0.4 target.

## 6. Release
- [ ] T6.1 Document the endpoint and the export schema.
- [ ] T6.2 Put it behind a feature flag and roll out gradually.
- [ ] T6.3 Add monitoring and alerts (latency, error rate, rate-limit hits).
- [ ] T6.4 Ship.

## Suggested order
T0 → T1 → T2 → T3 (in parallel with T4) → T5 → T6
```

Because "all of a user's data" is the scope, T3 (authorization, rate limiting, secrets exclusion) is the part I'd protect if time gets tight. Skipping it carries a real security risk, while the rest can be trimmed.
